subject: Pilot promo stacking & packaging clarification
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@launchpad.vc>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot credits + packaging question

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. Launchpad is lining up a six-company pilot cohort and we want to include a Redwood credit package as the compute incentive. Two quick asks before I send a formal mutual action plan: 

1) Can Redwood allow stacking of a one-time accelerator voucher (we give companies $5k each) with your usual promo credits so startups effectively get both for the first 30 days? We sometimes layer vouchers from us + your promo to make the runway feel more meaningful.

2) For the cohort, we usually negotiate a small packaging addendum: award 10 mentorship hours from the Redwood solutions team (20% of a TPM's time) tied to early usage milestones. Is that something you can carve into the promo agreement, even if it is non-billable?

Attached a short term sheet and our usage estimates so you can see expected consumption. If stacking is a hard no, tell me what the closest equivalent would be (e.g., increased promo amount, or guaranteed conversion credit).

Best,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Programs, Launchpad Ventures
attachment: accelerator-term-sheet.pdf (pdf)
attachment: launchpad-usage-projections.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@launchpad.vc>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot credits + packaging question

Hi Elaine — great to hear the cohort is moving forward, congrats. Quick answers and then a request for a short call: 

1) Stacking policy: we generally avoid direct stacking of external vouchers with our promo credits that convert to reserved capacity, because it creates accounting and entitlement complexity when customers convert to Dedicated. That said, we have two practical workarounds we've used for cohorts:
- Option A (preferred): keep both, but make the voucher (Launchpad) redeemable against the invoice and our promo applied as an additional line-item credit for 30 days. That keeps accounting clean and prevents double-counting on conversion.
- Option B: if you need a clean audit trail for investors, we can increase Redwood's promo pool for the cohort by 15% instead of stacking — effectively a larger promo that is fully managed by Redwood.

2) Mentorship hours: we can commit up to 10 mentorship hours delivered as structured office hours split across the cohort, but we typically treat that as a services addendum (non-recurring). We can include a short clause that the hours are contingent on reaching 10% of projected usage during the first 14 days.

Can Marissa join a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the term-sheet language and the accounting approach? If that works, we'll draft a one-paragraph packaging addendum for legal to sign off.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine@launchpad.vc>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits + packaging question

Connor — thanks for the clarity. Option A sounds workable; the cohort prefers to keep the voucher line visible on their invoices. We also prefer mentorship to be pre-baked into the pilot packet if possible (makes recruiting easier).

Two follow-ups:
- For Option A, can Redwood confirm that promo credits will not be clawed back if a startup later upgrades to Dedicated? Our founders want predictability around conversion credits.
- For mentorship, can you confirm the delivery model (group office hours vs 1:1) and an estimated timeline for scheduling?

A 30-minute call works Wednesday morning PST; Marissa on the thread is fine.

Elaine
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@launchpad.vc>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits + packaging question

Hi Elaine — thanks for the call today, appreciate the context. Quick summary of what we can commit to and what we'll formalize in the addendum: 

- Clawback on conversion: we will not retroactively remove promo credits that were applied during the 30-day pilot if a startup later purchases Dedicated. Promo credit accounting will be clearly documented on the invoice and in our billing metadata; legal will add an explicit "no-clawback on conversion" line.

- Mentorship delivery: we propose cohort-style office hours (2 x 90-minute sessions) led by Redwood solutions engineers (group format) + two 30-minute slots reserved for one-to-one triage available by application. We'll coordinate scheduling after acceptance.

- Documentation & ops: we'll attach a one-page packaging addendum to the pilot term sheet stating voucher stacking approach (Option A), conversion protection, mentorship scope, and the usage gate (10% projected usage within 14 days). Ben — finance, assigning to you to draft the invoice line-item wording and confirm how the promo will appear in HubSpot/ billing exports.

Action items: Marissa to send draft addendum by EOD Thu; Ben to confirm billing wording. Connor to circulate final doc for signature.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Launch Programs, Redwood Inference
attachment: pilot-packaging-addendum-draft.docx (docx stub)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@launchpad.vc>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits + packaging question

Elaine — quick billing note: the invoice will show two separate line items when Option A is used: 1) Launchpad voucher (applied as a payment/credit on the invoice from an external partner) and 2) Redwood promotional credit (applied as a non-taxable adjustment line for 30 days). On conversion, the promo will be treated as an applied credit and will not be clawed back; any reserved capacity discounts after conversion are separate and subject to the Dedicated contract.

I'll also add a short memo for your finance team describing how to reconcile the voucher vs promo in QuickBooks / accounting exports. If you'd like that memo in a PDF, I can attach it to the addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to the cohort.
Ben Carter
Director, Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
